transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... I'm pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract I'm working on have been tracking my revisions. They're actually planting errors in the datasets. It's to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes, but... I know what I'm looking at, and I know what they're doing.
Can you tell me more about how you know they’re planting errors and not just making honest mistakes?

Because I've been working with these kinds of models for decades. I know what an honest mistake looks like. But this... they are tracking my exact revisions. Whenever I update a file, these very specific errors are planted right in the sections I was just working on. It's done on purpose to ruin the projections and make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

The junior analysts, and even my wife, they keep telling me it's just version-control mistakes or some kind of system glitch. But they don't see the pattern. I know what I'm looking at, and it's not an accident.
Have you considered that others might not see this pattern because it’s not actually happening, even though you believe it is?

I mean... sure, I've asked myself that. You have to step back and wonder if you're just making something out of nothing. But then I go back and look at the data again, and it's undeniable. 

My wife, the junior analysts on the team... they just don't have the same eye for the math that I do. They see a discrepancy and just assume it's a version-control mistake and move on. But I'm telling you, it's not. The people on this contract are tracking my specific revisions. They are planting those exact errors in the datasets to force me out of my role and make it look like I can't lead the work. I know it sounds unbelievable to them, and maybe to you, but it is actually happening.
Have you ever experienced any sensations—like hearing voices, seeing things, or feeling something that others don’t seem to notice?

No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. It's really just what's happening with the data and the files at work. That's the only thing that's been going on.
Have you ever had any unusual beliefs or suspicions about things unrelated to your work, that others might find hard to believe or not understand?

No, nothing like that. Everything else in my life is... well, it's completely normal. I don't have any strange theories about my neighbors or, you know, the government or anything, if that's what you're asking. It's strictly just this specific situation with the contract and the models at work, because that's where the tampering is actually happening. Outside of the office, everything is perfectly fine.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that others might not share, even if they seemed completely obvious to you, outside of this work situation?

I think I just answered that, but... no. I really haven't. Like I said, I don't have any other suspicions about anything else in my life. 

It's just the data tampering at the office. Outside of that, my life is completely standard. I'm not a paranoid person, if that's what you're getting at. I just know what the math is showing me at work, and that's the only place this is happening.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about the data tampering might not be accurate, even though it feels certain to you?

Well... no, I don't think so. I know my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it’s just version-control mistakes. They think it's just a technical glitch or user error. But I'm pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions. They're actively planting errors in the datasets to make it look like I can’t lead the work. I know what the numbers should be, so... no, I don't think my belief is inaccurate. I'm just seeing what they're actually doing.

Even though others have tried to convince you that these errors might be version-control mistakes, have you been completely certain—without any doubt—that these changes are actually intentional sabotage by others?

Yes, I am. Completely certain. I know my wife and the junior analysts mean well when they keep telling me it’s just version-control mistakes, but... they just don't see the reality of it. I have no doubt at all. 

The people on that environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions, and they are actively planting those errors in the datasets. They are doing it on purpose to make it look like I can’t lead the work. So, yes, I am absolutely sure.

Can you explain exactly how you believe the people on the contract are tracking your revisions and planting errors? Are you able to understand how they’re doing it, or does it seem to happen in a way that doesn’t make sense logically?

Well, I... I don't really know exactly how they're doing it. I mean, they're not in my office, obviously. But the numbers change. I put in the correct data, I run the models, and then when I go back to it later, the values are different. 

I don't have proof of the exact mechanism they're using to get into the system. Maybe they have some backdoor access to the servers, or they're manipulating the cloud backups before it syncs. I just know that what I enter is correct, and what comes out later is wrong, and it's always wrong in a way that makes my analysis look flawed. So I don't know the technical steps they're taking, but the result is right there in the data.

Even though your wife and the junior analysts have tried to show you that these changes could be version-control mistakes, have you still remained completely certain—without any doubt—that these changes are intentional sabotage by others?

Yes, like I said a moment ago, I haven't changed my mind. I have absolutely no doubt. 

My wife and the junior analysts... well, they can keep trying to tell me it’s just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm looking at. The people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions, and they are actively planting errors in those datasets. They are doing it specifically to make it look like I can’t lead the work. So, yes, no matter what anyone else tries to show me, I am completely certain it's intentional sabotage.

Do you believe that the way the people on the contract are tracking your revisions and planting errors is something that could happen to anyone in your position, or is it specifically targeted at you in a way that doesn’t happen to others?

It is specifically targeted at me. Like I've been saying, the whole reason I'm here talking to you is because I know those people on the environmental modeling contract are coming after my work specifically. 

They want to make it look like I am the one who can't lead the project. It doesn't happen to anyone else's data. Even though my wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it's just normal version-control mistakes... it's not. They are tracking my specific revisions and planting those errors in the datasets just to ruin my credibility. It's a deliberate effort against me, not just a random glitch that happens to anyone.
Have you ever had the sense that this is happening only to you, that others aren't experiencing the same kind of targeting or interference with their work, even though they might be in similar roles?

Yeah, I mean... I feel like I just said this a second ago, but yes, it is absolutely just happening to me. 

If it were really just normal version-control mistakes, like my wife or those junior analysts keep trying to tell me, then everybody's numbers would be getting messed up. But they aren't. It's only my work. Those people on the environmental modeling contract are tracking my revisions specifically. They are only planting errors in my datasets because I'm the one in charge, and they want to make it look like I can't lead the work. Nobody else on the team is dealing with this interference, just me.
Can you explain why you believe the people on the contract are targeting you specifically with these errors?

Well, I'm here because I'm pretty sure... I mean, I know that they want my position. They want to take over the project. By tracking my revisions and planting those errors in the datasets, they can make it look like I can't lead the work. If my data is always wrong, it makes me look incompetent. That's the whole point. Even when my wife or the junior analysts tell me it’s just version-control mistakes, I know it's not. They're doing it to push me out.
Can you tell me who exactly you believe is planting these errors in your datasets?

Like I said before, it's the people on that environmental modeling contract. I don't necessarily have all their individual names in front of me, but it is that specific group of contractors. 

They are the ones getting in there, tracking my revisions, and planting the errors in the datasets. My wife and the junior analysts keep trying to tell me it’s just version-control mistakes, but I know it's those contractors doing it. They're the ones trying to make it look like I can't lead the work.
Do you believe the people on the contract have a personal motive against you, or are they acting with a specific kind of malice or agenda beyond just undermining your work?

I don't know if it's some deep personal malice, like they hate me as a person or something outside of the job. It's really just what I've been saying. Their agenda is getting my position. 

I'm pretty sure the people on that environmental modeling contract have been tracking my revisions and planting errors in the datasets for that one specific reason—to make it look like I can't lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep trying to tell me it’s just version-control mistakes, but I know what I'm looking at. It's a calculated move to get me out of the way so they can take over. That's the motive.
